subject: Supply Chain & Logistics
title: The Cost of Being Wrong
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Cost of Being Wrong.

hook.text: A retailer ordered 2 million units. Customers wanted 500,000. The rest went to landfill.

buildup.text: Bad forecasts cause two expensive problems: too much inventory or not enough to meet demand.

discovery.text: Overforecasting wastes cash on unsold stock. Underforecasting loses sales and frustrates customers.

twist.text: The average forecast error across industries is 30–50%. No forecast is ever perfectly right.

climax.text: Companies with strong demand planning reduce forecast error to 15–20% and save millions in waste.

punchline.text: Every forecast is wrong. The goal is to be less wrong.

quiz.question: What is the average forecast error across industries?
